open_decisions.question: The CURSMGR source is truncated after line 91: 'F' performs P300-FETCH-DATA THRU P300-EXIT (line 52) and 'C' performs P400-CLOSE-CURSOR THRU P400-EXIT (line 55), neither of which exists. Can the complete CURSMGR source be obtained, and what are the fetch and close behaviours (rows returned, end-of-data and response codes)?

Copybook SQLCA (FIL-0017) includes itself ('EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA' at line 6) and defines only SQL-STATUS-CODES, with no SQLCODE or SQLERRMC field; SQLCODE/SQLERRMC therefore have no Field ID in the 14 DB2 programs. Which SQLCA layout does the precompiler supply, and may the modern design assume the standard DB2 SQLCODE/SQLERRMC meaning (assumption ASM-004)?

Copybook SQLCA (SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0017) line 6 contains 'EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA END-EXEC', naming itself. The included SQL communication area (SQLCODE, SQLSTATE, SQLERRMC, ...) has no layout in any reverse artifact. How should the forward design obtain the SQLCA layout and the SQLCODE/SQLSTATE semantics used by the 14 DB2 programs?

The project SQLCA copybook (SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0017) includes itself and declares only SQL-STATUS-CODES, while eight packet programs test SQLCODE (and DB2ONLN SQLERRMC), which only the DB2 precompiler's SQLCA supplies. Should the Java design treat SQL status as coming from the SQL driver (SQLException/SQLState) and ignore the project SQLCA content, or must the 35-byte WS-DB2-AREA content be reproduced?

CURSMGR's fetch ('F') and close ('C') requests PERFORM P300-FETCH-DATA THRU P300-EXIT and P400-CLOSE-CURSOR THRU P400-EXIT, which are missing from the truncated source (ends at line 91). Can the complete CURSMGR source be supplied, or should fetch/close be specified from INQHIST's usage?

INQHIST moves the DB2 connection token to WS-DB2-TOKEN (line 125), which is declared nowhere, and never places the account number in the cursor request. How is the connection token carried to the cursor manager, and which account selects the history rows?
